subject: Acme evaluation & price match request — hosted API per-token & commit tiers
message_1_subject: Re: Redwood proposal — need price parity with incumbent endpoints
message_1_body:
Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the proposal — we reviewed with procurement and engineering. Two asks before we can move to legal: 1) Can Redwood match the per-token economics we're getting today from OpenAI/Anthropic cloud endpoints for generation and embeddings? Our current blended rate across generations and embeddings is ~$0.0048/token (volume-weighted). 2) We need clarity on committed tier pricing and what happens if we exceed the commit (true-up vs overage slab).

Specifically: if we commit to ~3B tokens/month (12 month term) what per-token price can you guarantee for both standard and long-context generation? Also please include any onboarding credits, ingress assistance for model conversion, and whether you will provide a migration plan that limits risk to our product roadmap.

Procurement has asked for a direct comparison matrix vs OpenAI and Anthropic that shows list price, committed price, and any caveats (regional egress, burst limits). Can you send that by EOD Friday?

Best,
Carlos
VP, Platform Engineering
Acme Corporation

On Thu, Oct 15, 2026 at 06:03 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Attached is our baseline proposal and a short comparison doc — happy to walk through.
message_2_subject: Re: Redwood proposal — committed tiers & comparison matrix attached
message_2_body:
Carlos — thanks for the clear asks. High level response and a few options below; attached is a refreshed proposal and a one-page comparison matrix that maps our pricing to the incumbents (acme-comparison-matrix.xlsx).

1) Commit tiers we can offer (blended per-token):
   - 0-1B tokens/mo: $0.0065 / token (on-demand)
   - 1B-3B tokens/mo (12mo commit): $0.0045 / token
   - 3B-6B tokens/mo (12mo commit): $0.0039 / token + prefix caching enabled by default

2) Introductory concession: we can provide a one-time migration credit equal to 2 weeks of expected spend and a free engineering migration consultation (3 days) to accelerate model conversion.

3) Exceeding commit: standard overage slab applies (next tier price) with monthly true-up. We can include a 30-day smoothing window for bursts so you won't be hit with short-term spikes.

4) Differentiators vs incumbents: workload-aware caching and KV prefix reuse can reduce token billable volume significantly on chat-heavy flows; our Console exposes token-level traceability so you can reconcile costs per route.

I'll ask pricing ops to run a modeled comparison using your sample traffic if you can share an anonymized week of token profiles. Can we get that by Friday? If you want a faster path to parity, we can do a temporary targeted discount while we validate the traffic profile.

Attached: redwood-proposal-v2.pdf, acme-comparison-matrix.xlsx

Next step: happy to schedule a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
message_3_subject: Fwd: Acme pricing asks — suggested concession & approval path
message_3_body:
Naomi — forwarding Acme thread with my suggested play. TL;DR: Acme is high-value, fast-close. Suggested concession to win: 1) Matching target blended rate of $0.0042/token for first 6 months (conditional on a 12-month commit of 3B tokens/month), 2) One-time $75k migration credit, 3) Dedicated onboarding SRE for 4 weeks.

Rationale: that gets us near parity they ask for, preserves upside after 6 months (we revert to committed slab), and keeps legal redlines minimal. Need pricing ops to confirm cost impact and finance sign-off for the migration credit. Karthik — can you confirm whether a 6-month promotional slab is within standard discount authority, or do we need Vivek sign-off for a migration credit of this size?

Also attached a suggested redlines list for procurement and a note on SLA language.

—Marissa

On Thu, Oct 15, 2026 at 10:38 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Carlos — draft reply below; sending with Marissa for approval.
message_4_subject: Re: Redwood proposal — committed tiers & comparison matrix attached
message_4_body:
Naomi / Marissa — appreciate the speed here. A few clarifications and counters:

1) The $0.0045 and $0.0039 slabs look promising. Our ask: a floor blended guarantee that locks in at $0.0042/token for the first 12 weeks from go-live (not 6 months) if we sign a 12-month 3B commit — that helps bridge our transition risk and simplifies procurement.

2) Migration credit: $75k is acceptable if you also commit to up to 4 SRE days during first 30 days post-launch and provide runbook handover.

3) Proof of parity: procurement needs a short annex listing any caveats (multi-region egress charges, model quantization differences, and burst throttling) and a sample invoice reconciliation for a representative month.

4) Contract: we'll need an explicit clause for data residency and an audit window. We can get legal to draft redlines once we have a commercial term sheet.

If you can confirm the 12-week promotional blended floor and give a draft term sheet (DocuSign preferred), we can route to procurement and legal this week.

—Carlos
message_5_subject: RE: Redwood proposal — draft term sheet & promotional floor confirmed
message_5_body:
Carlos — thanks. Per internal alignment: we can confirm the following final concessions if Acme signs the 12-month 3B tokens/mo commitment by Oct 22.

1) Promotional blended floor: $0.0042/token for the first 12 weeks post go-live.
2) Migration: $75k migration credit + up to 4 SRE days in the first 30 days + runbook handover.
3) Overage handling: monthly true-up to next slab; 30-day smoothing window on bursts.

Attaching refreshed proposal and a DocuSign link for a commercial term sheet (docusign-acme-nda.pdf). If procurement can confirm the anonymized week of token profiles we will run a final modeled invoice so legal/procurement can reconcile.

Vivek — looping you for sign-off on the migration credit and to confirm SLA exception for the one-time onboarding SRE. Approvals needed by EOD Oct 16 to meet Acme timeline.

Next steps: I'll send the DocuSign term sheet once Vivek confirms.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
